newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply off as weather fears ease.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply off as weather fears ease.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended sharply lower as speculators bailed out because the threat of cold in the citrus belt faded, traders and analysts said.
Buzz Lopez, a weather forecaster at Smith Barney, said there were no expectations of temperatures below freezing point in Florida's citrus belt over the next few days.
"It looks like a minimal threat," Lopez said.

With little immediate threat of frost, spot January FCOJ saw the biggest loss, ending down 3.15 cents at 76.00 cents a lb. Most active March closed down 2.25 cents at 77.85 cents, barely above the life-of-contract low of 77.80 cents hit during the session.
Volume was not particularly heavy at an estimated 3,800 lots, compared to Wednesday's official 2,942 lots.
With only a slim threat of cold weather, speculators who had bargained on damaging frost, bailed out, Celeste Georgakis, FCOJ specialist at Dean Witter Reynolds said.

The losses also followed USDA's Florida crop estimate, released early Thursday. The forecast for a 220 million box crop in 1996/97 and a yield of 1.53 gallons per box were unchanged from the Dept's December report.

"Everyone viewed the report as somewhat positive because they did not raise the estimate, but I think USDA are being conservative and along the way they will raise it," Georgakis said. "We will probably see a revision in the yields - they seem to be running at higher levels."
